chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Asbat ibn Salim said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We buy a 'Adl' (a bundle of fifty garments) for one hundred garments, and a man comes to us and takes seventy garments from the 'Adl' with a profit of one dirham per dirham. Should we sell the remainder at the same rate as we sold? He said: 'No, unless the garment is sold individually.'

key_terms.بِرِبْحِ دِرْهَمٍ دِرْهَمٍ: With a profit of one dirham per dirham (proportional profit)
key_terms.ٱلْعِدْل: A bundle or lot of fifty garments

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling the remaining items from a bulk bundle after a partial sale?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that when a buyer purchases a portion of a bulk commodity ('Adl') at a fixed profit rate, the seller cannot simply apply that same rate to the remainder; instead, the remaining items must be sold individually to ensure distinct valuation and avoid hidden uncertainty (gharar). This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on precision in commercial contracts, ensuring that partial sales do not inadvertently create inequity or ambiguity in the remaining goods' pricing structure.
